chapter: Danny's rise through New York bands to Cab Calloway
title: Wilbur De Paris never paid for the albums
summary: Danny made about six albums for Wilbur on a promise of payment and had to take him to the union after three years.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: On toilet paper. And just walked out the rehearsal, man. So you have all them kind of people... So he did a whole lot of things with... He was planning to record. So he recorded Doc Cheatham, and I made about six albums with the promise that he was going to pay them as he sold the records. And he took that money, and he gets that money... I said, "When are you going to pay us, Wilbur?" That went on for about three years. So finally, I had to bring it to the union. Because he didn't believe nobody should have no money at all. And no sense in going to him and ask him to let you have ten dollars. Like, he argued with me once(?) (?) the bandleader. "I don't have no cash."

So I didn't have no respect for him at all. The only bandleader in the existence of music that didn't believe a musician should have nothin'. When he takes the tips, and they allowed him to do that -- he wasn't gonna take mine.
